evidence_supplied.chunk:csf2.0:text:65a38d02bf94:
This appendix describes the Functions, Categories, and Subcategories of the CSF Core. Table 1 lists the CSF 2.0 Core Function and Category names and unique alphabetic identifiers. Each Function name in the table is linked to its portion of the appendix. The order of Functions, Categories, and Subcategories of the Core is not alphabetical; it is intended to resonate most with those charged with operationalizing risk management within an organization. The numbering of the Subcategories is intentionally not sequential; gaps in numbering indicate CSF 1.1 Subcategories that were relocated in CSF 2.0.
Table 1. CSF 2.0 Core Function and Category names and identifiers
Function Category Category Identifier
Govern (GV) Organizational Context GV.OC
Risk Management Strategy GV.RM
Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities GV.RR
Policy GV.PO
Oversight GV.OV
Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management GV.SC
Identify (ID) Asset Management ID.AM
Risk Assessment ID.RA
Improvement ID.IM
Protect (PR) Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control PR.AA
Awareness and Training PR.AT
Data Security PR.DS
Platform Security PR.PS
Technology Infrastructure Resilience PR.IR
Detect (DE) Continuous Monitoring DE.CM
Adverse Event Analysis DE.AE
Respond (RS) Incident Management RS.MA
Incident Analysis RS.AN
Incident Response Reporting and Communication RS.CO
Incident Mitigation RS.MI
Recover (RC) Incident Recovery Plan Execution RC.RP
Incident Recovery Communication RC.CO

answer.answer: The primary structural difference is that CSF 1.1 places Supply Chain Risk Management (ID.SC) within the Identify function, whereas CSF 2.0 moves it to the Govern function as Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (GV.SC). In CSF 1.1, the category description emphasizes establishing priorities, constraints, and risk tolerances to support risk decisions. In CSF 2.0, the category description emphasizes that processes are identified, established, managed, monitored, and improved by organizational stakeholders. The CSF 2.0 subcategories are more granular, covering specific aspects like program establishment (GV.SC-01), integration into enterprise risk management (GV.SC-03), supplier prioritization (GV.SC-04), contract requirements (GV.SC-05), due diligence (GV.SC-06), ongoing risk monitoring (GV.SC-07), incident planning inclusion (GV.SC-08), life-cycle monitoring (GV.SC-09), and post-agreement activities (GV.SC-10).

key_changes.statement: CSF 1.1 locates Supply Chain Risk Management in the Identify function (ID.SC), while CSF 2.0 locates it in the Govern function (GV.SC).
The CSF 1.1 category description focuses on establishing priorities, constraints, risk tolerances, and assumptions to support risk decisions.
The CSF 2.0 category description focuses on processes being identified, established, managed, monitored, and improved by organizational stakeholders.
CSF 2.0 introduces specific subcategories for supplier prioritization (GV.SC-04), contract integration (GV.SC-05), and due diligence (GV.SC-06) that are mapped to broader CSF 1.1 subcategories.
CSF 2.0 includes subcategories for post-agreement activities (GV.SC-10) and life-cycle monitoring (GV.SC-09) which are mapped to the general CSF 1.1 ID.SC-1 subcategory.

mappings.note: Category level mapping from CSF 2.0 Govern to CSF 1.1 Identify.
Program and policy establishment mapped to general process identification.
Roles and responsibilities mapped to workforce/third-party role establishment.
Integration into risk management mapped to supplier assessment processes.
Also listed as conceptually new in 2.0 in the official workbook.
Supplier prioritization mapped to supplier identification and assessment.
Contract requirements mapped to contractual measures.
Due diligence mapped to general process identification.
Ongoing risk monitoring mapped to supplier assessment.
Ongoing risk monitoring also mapped to routine assessments/audits.
Incident planning inclusion mapped to response/recovery planning with suppliers.
Life-cycle monitoring mapped to general process identification.
Post-agreement activities mapped to general process identification.
